cities.base: Downtown/Centro, near Plaza de la Independencia, for walkability to the sights and the Costanera
cities.name: Asuncion

places.name: Comedor tipico junto a la plaza
places.note: Basic family-run lunch spot serving asado, mandioca and sopa paraguaya, the kind of place with a daily set menu and no printed one. Honest, cheap, and the only real sit-down meal option in town.

places.name: Palacio de Lopez / Plaza de la Independencia
places.note: Exterior viewing only, it's a working government building with no public interior access, so treat it as a photo op and not a real visit.

places.name: Casa de la Independencia
places.note: Small colonial house where independence was plotted, worth the short visit for the scale of it rather than the exhibits.

places.name: Mercado Cuatro
places.note: A real working market, good for lunch and browsing, not curated for visitors.

places.name: Recoleta Cemetery
places.note: Above-ground mausoleums, a quiet walk rather than a headline sight.

places.name: Costanera de Asuncion
places.note: The riverfront walk for an easy first evening after landing.

places.name: Trinidad ruins
places.note: The largest and best preserved of the Jesuit missions, the actual reason to route through this region.

places.name: Jesus de Tavarangue ruins
places.note: Smaller and unfinished compared to Trinidad, paired with it on the same day for the drive between them.

places.name: San Cosme y Damian ruins and observatory
places.note: The smaller Jesuit ruin, notable for the old observatory angle, further out and lower key than Trinidad.

places.name: Palacio de López / Plaza de la Independencia
places.note: Exterior viewing only, working government building with no public interior access. Photo op, not a real visit.

places.name: Casa de la Independencia
places.note: Small colonial house where independence conspirators met in 1811. Modest and quiet, worth the half hour, closes early afternoon and shuts Sundays.

places.name: Mercado Cuatro
places.note: Sprawling working market, not built for visitors. Good cheap lunch stalls and a real look at how the city shops, watch your bag.

places.name: Cementerio de la Recoleta
places.note: Above-ground mausoleums and family tombs of the old elite, some crumbling. A quieter, stranger stop than the more famous Recoleta in Buenos Aires.

places.name: Costanera de Asunción
places.note: Riverfront promenade along the Paraguay River, good for an evening walk with families and joggers out. Not much shade midday, better after 5pm.

places.name: Manzana de la Rivera
places.note: Cluster of restored colonial houses telling the city's history, next to the Palacio. Free entry, low key, easy to combine with the plaza.

places.name: Panteón Nacional de los Héroes
places.note: Small domed mausoleum for national military heroes, guards on rotation outside. Quick stop, five minutes from Casa de la Independencia.

places.name: Catedral Metropolitana de Asunción
places.note: Plain cathedral facing Plaza de la Independencia, unremarkable interior. Fine to glance at on the way past, not worth a special trip.

places.name: Lido Bar
places.note: Counter diner facing Plaza de los Héroes since the 1950s, order the sopa paraguaya or milanesa. A real Asunción institution, not a recreation of one.

places.name: Mburicaó (barrio) evening stroll
places.note: Leafy residential streets popular with locals for an evening walk or run, quieter and greener than downtown. Optional, mainly for a second evening in the city.

places.name: Mercado Central (Mercado Modelo)
places.note: Smaller and more manageable than Mercado Cuatro, good for ao po'i embroidery and ñandutí lace souvenirs without the chaos.

places.name: Loma San Jerónimo
places.note: Skip unless with a local guide. Colorful painted hillside barrio much photographed for tourism promotion but genuinely a poor neighborhood, the staged photo-op feel outweighs the visit for most travelers.

places.name: Santísima Trinidad de Paraná (Jesuit Ruins of Trinidad)
places.note: UNESCO site and the best preserved of the Jesuit reductions in Paraguay. Stone carvings on the church facade and the pulpit remnants are the highlight. Comes alive with almost no crowds compared to the scale of the ruins, worth the full ticket time rather than rushing through.

places.name: Museo de Sitio Trinidad
places.note: Small on-site museum included with the ruins ticket. A handful of recovered stone pieces and some context panels, not a destination on its own but worth the ten minutes on the way in or out.

places.name: Jesus de Tavarangue
places.note: Unfinished sister site to Trinidad, the church was never completed so you see the arches and stonework raw and unroofed. Combined ticket with Trinidad usually covers both. Quieter than Trinidad and worth the short drive between the two.

places.name: Artisan stalls at Trinidad entrance
places.note: A few stands selling local crafts and ao po'i embroidery near the entrance gate. Low pressure, fine for a five minute browse before or after the ruins, not worth a special trip.

places.name: Trinidad town center
places.note: Skip. This is a small rural crossroads town that exists to serve the ruins, there is nothing to see beyond the archaeological site itself and you will have covered everything in the itinerary already.

places.name: Local panadería near Trinidad ruins entrance
places.note: Simple bakery stop for chipa and cocido before starting the ruins. No sit-down restaurant scene in Trinidad itself, most visitors eat back in Encarnación.

places.name: Comedor near Jesus de Tavarangue parking area
places.note: Basic roadside comedor serving asado and milanesa plates for the lunch break between the two ruin sites. Nothing fancy, functional and cheap, order what's on the board rather than expecting a menu.

places.name: Cementerio de la reducción, Trinidad ruins
places.note: Part of the main Trinidad complex, the old mission cemetery layout is included in the walk through the ruins. Included in the main visit, not a separate stop.

places.name: Talleres (workshop quarters), Trinidad ruins
places.note: The residential and workshop foundations surrounding the main church, less photographed but gives the clearest sense of how the reduction actually functioned as a self sufficient community.

places.name: Walk around the grounds, Trinidad ruins
places.note: Grassy grounds around the church with old trees and open sightlines back to the reservation, pleasant to loop before heading back to the car, no shade in the middle of the day so mornings are more comfortable.

places.name: Late afternoon light on Trinidad church facade
places.note: Same site as the main ruins visit but the stone carvings on the west facing facade catch warmer light in late afternoon if your schedule allows a return pass before closing, not essential if you already saw it in the morning.

places.name: Ruinas Jesuiticas de Jesus de Tavarangue
places.note: Unfinished Jesuit reduction church, never completed so the arches and stonework are exposed in a way Trinidad isn't. Smaller and quieter than Trinidad, usually just you and a caretaker. The carved stone doorway is the single best piece of Jesuit stonework in the area.

places.name: Sacristia y Museo de Sitio
places.note: Small on-site museum room with fragments, maps and explanation of the reduction system. Included with ruins ticket. Skip if you've already done the Trinidad museum, it covers the same ground with less material.

places.name: Campanario de Jesus de Tavarangue
places.note: Freestanding bell tower structure near the main church ruin, part of the same complex ticket. Worth the extra ten minutes for the angle back toward the main facade.

places.name: Plaza de Jesus de Tavarangue
places.note: Ordinary small-town plaza across from the ruins entrance. Nothing special, just a place to sit before or after the site and watch the town rather than the ruins.

places.name: Parroquia Sagrada Familia
places.note: The town's working parish church, modern and modest, useful only as contrast to show what replaced the Jesuit-era building. Not worth a special trip on its own.

places.name: Puesto de Artesania local, frente a las ruinas
places.note: Small stall selling local crafts and ceramics near the ruins entrance, inconsistent hours depending on whether anyone's tending it that day. Fine for a quick look, not worth planning around.

places.name: Mirador natural cerca del arroyo
places.note: Unmarked rural viewpoint over the countryside a short walk from the town center, reachable on foot or by mototaxi. No facilities, no signage, just quiet farmland views. Only for travelers who want to stretch their legs after the ruins.

places.name: Torre mirador reconstruida (replica lookout)
places.note: Skip. A modern reconstructed lookout structure sometimes pointed out near the entrance, it adds nothing historically and the view from ground level is the same.

places.name: Despensa central del pueblo
places.note: Small general store on the main street for water and snacks before the ruins. No tourist infrastructure here, cash only, the owner is usually the only one who speaks any English at all in town.

places.name: Cruce de rutas hacia Trinidad
places.note: Skip. Just the highway junction between the two ruin sites, sometimes mentioned as a stop because of a small sign. Not worth stopping the car for.

places.name: Ruinas Jesuiticas de Jesus de Tavarangue, visita de tarde
places.note: Same site as the morning visit but worth a second pass late in the day if you're staying overnight nearby, the low light on the red sandstone facade is markedly better than midday. Requires the site to still be open or viewable from outside the fence, check closing time before planning this.

places.name: Ruinas Jesuiticas de San Cosme y Damian
places.note: Smaller and quieter than Trinidad, less restored, guided visit included in ticket and usually necessary to get into the buildings.

places.name: Observatorio Astronomico Jesuitico
places.note: Reconstructed sundial and star-alignment stonework on the same grounds as the ruins, this is the detail that sets this site apart from the other reducciones, worth asking the guide to explain in full.

places.name: Planetario Municipal
places.note: Small, low-budget planetarium tied to the observatory theme, only worth it if it's actually open and staffed that day, which is not guaranteed.

places.name: Costanera / riverfront on the Rio Parana
places.note: Quiet stretch of riverbank, good for stretching legs after the ruins visit, nothing organized, just the view and some fishermen.

places.name: Plaza principal de San Cosme y Damian
places.note: Ordinary small-town plaza, fine for a coffee stop or to sit while waiting on transport back to Encarnacion.

places.name: Comedor tipico near the ruins entrance
places.note: Simple set-menu Paraguayan food, chipa guasu and asado type dishes, options are limited so don't expect a menu, just eat what's offered.

places.name: Mirador junto al observatorio
places.note: Small raised viewpoint over the ruins footprint, decent for photos of the layout, not a proper lookout over the river or town.

places.name: Puesto de artesania local (guaicuru/ceramica)
places.note: Small stall selling local pottery and woven pieces tied to the mission's craft tradition, inventory is thin and inconsistent.

places.name: Puerto Ganchos (river port area)
places.note: Skip: a working cargo port, not scenic, only relevant if you have a specific boat connection, otherwise adds nothing to the day.

places.name: Ruinas de Santa Rosa de Lima (day trip extension)
places.note: Skip on this itinerary: another Jesuit site further from Encarnacion, technically visitable but would turn the day trip into a two-site slog and the traveller has already seen Trinidad and Jesus, this is diminishing returns.

outings.why: The two Jesuit mission ruins, done together as a full day including the drive between them.
outings.name: Trinidad and Jesus de Tavarangue

outings.why: The smaller Jesuit ruin with the old observatory, further out and lower key than Trinidad.
outings.name: San Cosme y Damian day trip
outings.fallback: Skip it and do the Encarnacion riverfront and market instead if you're tired.

destination.name: Paraguay
destination.pitch: A week for the Jesuit ruins around Encarnación and a capital city with no tourist infrastructure at all, which some people find refreshing and others find exhausting by day four.
destination.caveat: There is very little built for tourists here, so days can feel like logistics rather than sightseeing. Put together for you just now from what I know, rather than checked against today's opening times. Worth confirming anything you're pinning the trip on.

because.city: Asuncion is a working capital with almost no tourist gloss on it, which is its own kind of interesting.
because.food: Mercado Cuatro is a real market, not a curated one.
because.culture: The Jesuit ruins at Trinidad and Jesus de Tavarangue are the real reason to come.
because.exploration: San Cosme y Damian and the ruins circuit reward people who like figuring things out on the ground.
